ops.title: Regenerate the package table as the LAST step before pushing, not before the code lands
ops.body:
The `Docs drift` job (`scripts/gen-package-table.sh --check`) went red twice in one session, both times self-inflicted, both times for a different reason. Recording both so the next agent pays neither cost.

## Trap 1 — three copies, one command

`scripts/gen-package-table.sh` writes the table to **three** targets: `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `.claude/fragments/AGENTS.md/daemonkit-development-guide.fragment.md`. A path-scoped `ccx vcs ship … AGENTS.md` commits one of them and leaves the other two dirty, so the gate stays red. Commit all three together.

## Trap 2 — `AGENTS.md` is a render, so commit order matters

`AGENTS.md` opens with `<!-- GENERATED by cc-guides from .claude/fragments/AGENTS.md/ — do not edit -->`. It is **not** a source file. Committing the regenerated `AGENTS.md` *before* its fragment means the next cc-guides render reads the still-stale committed fragment and puts the old counts straight back — which looks exactly like the generator not working. Land the fragment first, or land all three in one commit.

## The actual lesson: sequence, not mechanics

The table encodes **per-package file and line counts**, so *any* code change moves it. Regenerating early and then landing more code re-breaks it immediately — which is what happened here: the table was regenerated, four code commits landed on top, and every count drifted again (`proc` 12340 → 12697, `service` 10596 → 10991, `wire` gained a file).

**Run the generator as the final step before pushing, after all code commits are in place**, and commit all three targets in one go. The check is cheap and definitive:

```
./scripts/gen-package-table.sh          # writes all three
./scripts/gen-package-table.sh --check  # exit 0 means clean
```

Note `--check` is the verification flag; the script's only other flag is bare invocation for write. There is no `--write`.
